fertilisation occurs outside the body in a laboratory, and the embryo is then implanted into the uterus
IVF permanently alters the genetic makeup of the offspring

IVF involves fertilisation in the fallopian tube Correct Answer: B Explanation: In IVF, egg cells are retrieved from the ovaries, fertilised with sperm in a laboratory dish ('in vitro' = in glass), and the resulting embryo(s) are transferred into the uterus for implantation. Why the other options are wrong: • A. IVF uses the same egg and sperm cells as natural fertilisation. C. IVF does not inherently alter genes (though preimplantation genetic diagnosis can screen for genetic disorders). D. Natural fertilisation occurs in the fallopian tube; IVF fertilisation occurs in the laboratory.

subject: Biology
question: The process by which gametes are formed through meiosis is called
options: cleavage Correct Answer: B Explanation: Gametogenesis is the production of gametes (sex cells) through meiosis. In males, it is spermatogenesis (producing sperm); in females, oogenesis (producing eggs). Why the other options are wrong: • A. Mitosis produces somatic (body) cells, not gametes. C. Fertilisation is the fusion of gametes, not their production. D. Cleavage is the rapid mitotic divisions of the zygote after fertilisation.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is an example of an out-breeding strategy in agriculture?
options: Mating siblings of the same pure breed repeatedly
Crossing two different established breeds to produce offspring with hybrid vigour (heterosis)
Self-pollinating a plant for multiple generations

Cloning an organism through vegetative propagation Correct Answer: B Explanation: Out-breeding (cross-breeding or hybridisation) involves mating unrelated individuals, often of different breeds or varieties. It exploits heterosis (hybrid vigour) — offspring are often larger, healthier, or more productive than either parent. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Mating siblings is inbreeding. C. Self-pollination for multiple generations is extreme inbreeding. D. Cloning maintains the same genotype — it is neither inbreeding nor outbreeding.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following best describes the phenotypic expression of a codominant trait?
options: Only the dominant allele is expressed in the phenotype
Neither allele is expressed — a completely new trait appears
Both alleles are fully expressed simultaneously in the heterozygote

The recessive allele is partially expressed in heterozygotes Correct Answer: C Explanation: In codominance, both alleles are equally and fully expressed in the heterozygote. Example: Blood group AB — both IA and IB are expressed, producing A and B antigens on red blood cells simultaneously. Why the other options are wrong: • A. That describes simple dominant-recessive inheritance. B. This describes incomplete dominance (a blended phenotype), not codominance. D. Partial expression of the recessive allele describes incomplete dominance.

subject: Biology
question: Identical (monozygotic) twins arise from
options: two eggs fertilised by two different sperm
one egg fertilised by two sperm
one fertilised egg that splits into two embryos

two eggs fertilised by the same sperm Correct Answer: C Explanation: Monozygotic (identical) twins develop when a single fertilised egg (zygote) splits completely into two separate embryos at an early developmental stage. They share identical DNA. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Two eggs fertilised by two sperm produce fraternal (dizygotic) twins. B. One egg fertilised by two sperm is not a normal developmental pathway. D. Two eggs cannot be fertilised by the same single sperm.

subject: Biology
question: Phenylthiocarbamide (PTC) tasting ability demonstrates
options: continuous variation in the human population
discontinuous variation — individuals are either tasters or non-tasters

environmentally induced variation Correct Answer: C Explanation: PTC tasting is a classic example of discontinuous variation. The ability to taste PTC (bitter) is controlled by the TAS2R38 gene. Individuals are distinctly either tasters (dominant allele) or non-tasters (recessive homozygote) — no intermediate. Why the other options are wrong: • A. PTC tasting has two discrete phenotype classes — no continuous range. B. The TAS2R38 gene is autosomal (chromosome 7), not sex-linked. D. PTC tasting is genetically determined, not environmentally induced. SECTION E: EVOLUTION

subject: Biology
question: Lamarck's theory of evolution is based on the concept of
options: inheritance of acquired characteristics through use and disuse of organs

geographical isolation leading to speciation Correct Answer: B Explanation: Lamarck proposed that organs used extensively develop and enlarge (use) while unused organs shrink (disuse), and these acquired changes are inherited by offspring. Though largely discredited, it was an important early evolutionary theory. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Natural selection and random mutations are Darwin's mechanism. C. Genetic recombination is part of modern evolutionary theory. D. Geographic isolation is a concept in allopatric speciation, not Lamarck's framework.

subject: Biology
question: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection states that
options: organisms acquire new traits during their lifetime and pass them to offspring
individuals with traits better suited to their environment survive and reproduce more successfully
all species were created in their current form and do not change

evolution is always directed toward complexity Correct Answer: B Explanation: Darwin's natural selection: heritable variation exists in populations; those individuals with advantageous traits survive and reproduce more ('survival of the fittest'). Their traits become more common over generations, leading to evolutionary change. Why the other options are wrong: • A. This is Lamarck's concept of inheritance of acquired characteristics. C. This is the creationist/fixity of species view, which evolution directly challenges. D. Evolution is not inherently directed toward complexity — it adapts organisms to their environment.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following provides the best evidence that modern whales evolved from land- dwelling ancestors?
options: Whales produce milk for their young

Whales are warm-blooded Correct Answer: B Explanation: Vestigial pelvic bones in whales are remnants of a hind-limb structure from their terrestrial ancestor. These non-functional skeletal remnants are strong anatomical evidence of evolutionary descent from land mammals. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Breathing with lungs is consistent with evolution from land ancestors, but vestigial bones are more direct anatomical evidence. C. Producing milk is a mammalian characteristic — consistent with ancestry but not specific evidence of terrestrial origins. D. Being warm-blooded is a general mammalian trait.

subject: Biology
question: Fossil records provide evidence for evolution because they
options: show that all organisms were created simultaneously
demonstrate that organisms have remained unchanged throughout geological time
reveal a progression of increasingly complex organisms in successive geological layers

prove that environmental changes have no effect on organisms Correct Answer: C Explanation: Fossil records show that older rock layers contain simpler life forms and younger layers contain more complex organisms. The succession of forms in geological strata documents evolutionary transitions and change over time. Why the other options are wrong: • A. The fossil record shows change over time — evidence against simultaneous creation. B. Organisms have clearly changed — different fossils appear in different geological periods. D. The fossil record actually shows responses to environmental change (mass extinctions, adaptive radiations).

subject: Biology
question: The concept of organic evolution is best defined as
options: the development of an individual organism from embryo to adult
the sum total of all adaptive changes in populations over long periods, resulting in diversity of life
the genetic changes within a single individual during its lifetime

the process of growth and development from birth to maturity Correct Answer: B Explanation: Organic evolution refers to the gradual change in heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations through processes such as natural selection, mutation, genetic drift, and gene flow — resulting in the diversity of all life on Earth. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Development of an individual (ontogeny) is not evolution. C. Evolution occurs in populations, not individuals. D. Growth from birth to maturity is development, not evolution.

subject: Biology
question: Comparative anatomy provides evidence for evolution through the existence of
options: identical functions of all organs across species
homologous structures — same basic structure but different functions
no similarities between distantly related species

organs that perform identical functions and have identical structures Correct Answer: B Explanation: Homologous structures (e.g. the forelimb bones of humans, whales, bats, and horses) have the same basic skeletal arrangement but are modified for different functions. This similarity suggests common ancestry. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Organs do not have identical functions across all species. C. Distantly related species do share certain anatomical similarities due to common ancestry. D. Analogous structures (e.g. wings of birds and insects) have similar functions but different structures — not evidence of common ancestry.

subject: Biology
question: A mutation is best defined as
options: a change in the behaviour of an organism in response to its environment
a heritable change in the nucleotide sequence of DNA
the passing of acquired traits from parent to offspring

a temporary change in phenotype caused by environmental stress Correct Answer: B Explanation: A mutation is a permanent, heritable change in the DNA sequence. It can involve a single base (point mutation) or larger chromosomal rearrangements. Mutations are the ultimate source of all new genetic variation in populations. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Behavioural changes are not mutations — they are acquired traits. C. Passing acquired traits is Lamarckism (not the accepted mechanism). D. Temporary phenotypic changes are not mutations — they are not heritable.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is a correct contribution of Darwin to evolutionary theory?
options: He discovered the DNA double helix structure
He proposed the mechanism of natural selection as the driving force of evolution
He developed the concept of mutation and gene theory

He classified organisms into kingdoms using binomial nomenclature Correct Answer: B Explanation: Darwin's key contribution was the theory of evolution by natural selection — published in 'On the Origin of Species' (1859). He argued that heritable variation + differential survival/reproduction = evolutionary change. Why the other options are wrong: • A. DNA double helix was discovered by Watson and Crick (1953). C. Mutation theory was developed by Hugo de Vries; gene theory by Thomas Hunt Morgan and others. D. Binomial nomenclature was developed by Carl Linnaeus.

subject: Biology
question: Analogous structures, such as the wings of birds and insects, are evidence of
options: convergent evolution — similar function in unrelated organisms
divergent evolution from the same ancestor

genetic recombination Correct Answer: B Explanation: Analogous structures are functionally similar but anatomically different structures that evolved independently in unrelated lineages to perform the same function (convergent evolution). They do NOT suggest common ancestry. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Homologous structures (same anatomy, different function) suggest common ancestry. C. Divergent evolution from a common ancestor produces homologous structures. D. Genetic recombination is a mechanism of variation within a population, not related to analogous structures.

subject: Biology
question: Industrial melanism in the peppered moth (Biston betularia) is a classic example of
options: Lamarckian evolution — moths becoming darker due to coal dust
natural selection — dark moths had a survival advantage on soot-covered bark
sexual selection — females preferred darker males

genetic drift in a small population Correct Answer: B Explanation: Before industrialisation, light-coloured moths were camouflaged on lichen-covered bark and were less visible to predators. Industrial pollution killed lichens and darkened bark with soot. Dark (melanic) moths then had a survival advantage, were less predated, and became more common — natural selection. Why the other options are wrong: • A. The moths did not become dark because of individual use/need — the dark mutation already existed; selection increased its frequency. C. Sexual selection involves mate choice — predation by birds was the selection pressure here. D. Genetic drift occurs in very small populations due to chance — this was directed selection in a large population.

subject: Biology
question: Vestigial organs are important evidence for evolution because they
options: are fully functional in all species that possess them
are remnants of structures that were functional in ancestral organisms, suggesting evolutionary history
always increase in size through generations due to use

appear only in extinct organisms found in the fossil record Correct Answer: B Explanation: Vestigial structures (e.g. human appendix, coccyx, ear muscles, whale pelvic bones) are reduced, non-functional remnants of structures that were functional in evolutionary ancestors. Their presence reveals evolutionary history and descent with modification. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Vestigial organs are non-functional (or reduced in function) in current organisms. C. Vestigial organs tend to reduce in size over evolutionary time (as selection does not maintain them). D. Vestigial organs are found in living organisms, not only in fossils.

subject: Biology
question: Comparative embryology supports evolution because it shows that
options: embryos of all species are identical throughout development
distantly related vertebrates share similar embryonic stages, suggesting common ancestry
embryos develop in opposite patterns in related species

embryo structure is entirely determined by the environment Correct Answer: B Explanation: Vertebrate embryos (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals) show striking similarities in early developmental stages (gill slits, tail structures, somites). These shared features suggest common ancestry — embryonic similarities persist because of shared ancestral developmental genes. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Embryos diverge as development proceeds — they are not identical throughout. C. Related species show convergent early embryonic patterns, not opposite patterns. D. Embryo development is primarily genetically determined, not environmental.

subject: Biology
question: The modern synthetic theory of evolution (neo-Darwinism) combines
options: Lamarck's use and disuse with Mendel's genetics
Darwin's natural selection with Mendelian genetics, population genetics, and molecular biology
Darwin's theory with Lamarck's inheritance of acquired characteristics

geology and comparative anatomy only Correct Answer: B Explanation: The Modern Synthesis (neo-Darwinism) integrates Darwin's natural selection with Mendel's genetics, population genetics (Hardy-Weinberg), molecular biology (mutations in DNA), and palaeontology, providing a comprehensive mechanistic explanation of evolution. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Lamarck's use and disuse is not part of the Modern Synthesis (it was largely discredited). C. Lamarckian inheritance is not included in neo-Darwinism. D. The Modern Synthesis incorporates genetics and molecular biology, not just geology and anatomy.

subject: Biology
question: Speciation is best defined as
options: a change in the frequency of one allele in a population
the process by which new species arise from pre-existing species, usually through reproductive isolation

the development of new traits in an individual organism Correct Answer: B Explanation: Speciation is the evolutionary process by which populations diverge to become distinct species, typically involving reproductive isolation (geographical, behavioural, or temporal) preventing gene flow, allowing independent evolution. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Allele frequency change is microevolution — it does not necessarily lead to speciation. C. Extinction is the opposite of speciation. D. Trait development in an individual is development, not speciation.

subject: Biology
question: Natural selection acts on
options: the phenotype of individuals in a population

all individuals in a population equally Correct Answer: B Explanation: Natural selection acts on observable phenotypes — it is the expressed traits that determine survival and reproduction. An individual with a beneficial phenotype (regardless of its exact genotype) is more likely to survive and reproduce, passing on the underlying genes. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Selection cannot directly 'see' the genotype; it acts on phenotype. C. DNA is the inherited material, but selection operates through phenotypic effects. D. Selection is differential — individuals differ in survival and reproduction.

subject: Biology
question: Geographical isolation promotes speciation because it
options: allows unlimited gene flow between separated populations
prevents interbreeding between populations, allowing independent divergence
increases mutation rate in isolated populations

accelerates reproduction in isolated populations Correct Answer: B Explanation: When populations are geographically separated (by mountains, oceans, rivers), gene flow stops. Each population is subject to different selective pressures, mutations, and genetic drift, causing them to diverge genetically until they are reproductively incompatible — separate species. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Geographical barriers prevent gene flow. C. Geographical isolation does not inherently increase mutation rate. D. Isolation may actually reduce population size (bottleneck effect) rather than accelerate reproduction.

subject: Biology
question: The occurrence of similar proteins (e.g. cytochrome c) in organisms from different taxonomic groups is evidence of
options: common ancestry and evolution from shared ancestors
horizontal gene transfer only in plants

the fixity of species Correct Answer: B Explanation: Cytochrome c (involved in cellular respiration) is found in virtually all aerobic organisms. Differences in the amino acid sequence between species correlate with evolutionary distance — organisms sharing more recent common ancestors have more similar cytochrome c sequences. This molecular evidence supports common descent. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Convergent evolution produces functionally similar but structurally different results — cytochrome c similarity in related organisms indicates shared ancestry. C. Horizontal gene transfer occurs in bacteria; it does not explain universal cytochrome c similarity across all life. D. Molecular similarity across species contradicts fixity of species.

subject: Biology
question: The peppered moth example demonstrates that natural selection is
options: directional, favouring traits that improve survival in a given environment
always stabilising, maintaining the average phenotype

only sexual selection Correct Answer: B Explanation: The peppered moth case shows directional selection — the environment (soot-darkened trees) favoured darker moths because they were less visible to bird predators. The frequency of dark moths increased rapidly, demonstrating selection acting in a specific direction. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Natural selection is not random — it differentially favours certain phenotypes. C. Stabilising selection maintains the average (e.g. human birth weight); directional selection shifts the average. D. The peppered moth example is driven by predation, not mate choice.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following scenarios demonstrates genetic drift?
options: Antibiotics kill most bacteria in a population; resistant bacteria survive and reproduce
In a small isolated population, certain alleles become common or disappear by chance
Sexual selection drives the evolution of elaborate peacock tail feathers

New plant species arise due to polyploidy Correct Answer: B Explanation: Genetic drift is random change in allele frequencies in a population due to chance events, not natural selection. It has the greatest effect in small populations, where random sampling can dramatically change allele frequencies. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Bacteria surviving antibiotics is natural selection (directional). C. Peacock tail feathers are driven by sexual selection (non-random). D. Polyploidy-driven speciation is a form of sympatric speciation.

subject: Biology
question: The presence of gill pouches (pharyngeal arches) in human embryos is evidence that
options: humans breathe through gills as adults
humans share a common ancestor with fish and other aquatic vertebrates

humans evolved from amphibians only Correct Answer: B Explanation: Pharyngeal (gill) arches in early human embryos are a developmental remnant of ancestral fish. Their presence in all vertebrate embryos (though they develop into different structures in each class) is strong evidence of common vertebrate ancestry. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Humans develop lungs — gill pouches don't become functional gills. C. Human embryos develop in amniotic fluid, not water; the presence of gill pouches is a genetic evolutionary remnant. D. Gill pouches suggest ancestry beyond amphibians — back to fish.

subject: Biology
question: Darwin observed that finches on the Galapagos Islands had diverse beak shapes. This diversity is best explained by
options: Lamarckian use and disuse — birds used their beaks differently and passed on the shapes
adaptive radiation — finches from a common ancestor diversified to exploit different food sources on different islands
random mutation only, without any selection

interbreeding with mainland South American finches regularly Correct Answer: B Explanation: Galapagos finches underwent adaptive radiation — descendants of a common ancestor colonised different islands with different food resources (seeds, insects, cactus) and evolved different beak shapes suited to each food source through natural selection. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Beak shape is genetically inherited — Lamarckian use-and-disuse is discredited. C. Mutations provide variation, but selection directed the specific beak shapes for particular ecological niches. D. The islands are isolated from the mainland, preventing regular interbreeding.

subject: Biology
question: The geological time scale provides evidence for evolution because
options: fossils from all geological periods show identical organisms
older geological layers contain fossils of simpler organisms, with more complex forms appearing in younger layers
the time scale shows that the Earth is only 6,000 years old

most fossils are found at the Earth's surface Correct Answer: B Explanation: The geological time scale records the history of life through rock strata. Older, deeper layers contain simple organisms (bacteria, algae in Precambrian); younger layers show increasingly complex organisms (fish in Devonian, mammals in Cenozoic), documenting evolutionary progression over billions of years. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Fossils in different periods show different organisms — evidence of change. C. Scientific dating methods (radiometric) show Earth is ~4.5 billion years old. D. Most significant fossils are found in sedimentary rock layers deep below the surface.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is NOT a mechanism of evolution?
options: Mutation Correct Answer: C Explanation: Mitosis is the process of cell division for growth and repair, producing genetically identical daughter cells. It does not cause changes in allele frequencies in populations and therefore is NOT an evolutionary mechanism. Mutation, natural selection, genetic drift, and gene flow are the recognised mechanisms of evolution. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Natural selection is the primary mechanism of adaptive evolution. B. Genetic drift causes random allele frequency changes. D. Mutation is the ultimate source of new genetic variation.

subject: Biology
question: Convergent evolution is best illustrated by
options: the similar forelimb bones of humans, bats, and whales
the wings of bats (mammals) and wings of birds — similar function, different structure
the gradual increase in horse body size over 50 million years

the similar DNA sequences of humans and chimpanzees Correct Answer: B Explanation: Convergent evolution occurs when unrelated organisms independently evolve similar adaptations to similar environments. Bat wings and bird wings both enable flight but evolved independently from different ancestral forelimb structures. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Similar forelimb bones in humans, bats, and whales are homologous structures — evidence of divergent evolution from a common ancestor. C. Horse evolution is an example of directional evolution (phyletic gradualism). D. Similar DNA in humans and chimps reflects common ancestry (divergent evolution).

subject: Physics
question: A student measures the diameter of a wire using a micrometer screw gauge and records 2.35 mm. The pitch of the screw gauge is 0.5 mm and has 50 divisions. What is the least count of this instrument?
options: 0.001 mm ✓ Correct Answer: A Explanation: Least count = Pitch / Number of divisions = 0.5 mm / 50 = 0.01 mm. This is the smallest measurement the micrometer can accurately make. Why others are wrong: B: 0.05 mm is the pitch divided by 10, not 50. C: 0.5 mm is just the pitch, not the least count. D: 0.001 mm is too small for a standard micrometer.

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following is a fundamental (base) physical quantity?
options: Pressure ✓ Correct Answer: C Explanation: Electric current (measured in Amperes) is one of the seven SI fundamental quantities. Velocity (m/s), force (kg·m/s²), and pressure (N/m²) are all derived quantities. Why others are wrong: A: Velocity = displacement/time — derived from length and time. B: Force = mass × acceleration — derived. D: Pressure = force/area — derived.

subject: Physics
